scope: Recover three reverse-array cursor paths in two original card units: Pia Revolution helper/card arrays of20/22 target_t entries and Out of Time marked[151][2] int matrix. Use the actual array plus count minus one instead of address arithmetic from unrelated scalar locals; keep all native capacities, collection code, ordering, flags, dialog/ownership logic and counter counts. Skip the final unused cursor decrement so the C pointer remains within its array; exact source replay verifies that no later source operation uses that cursor. Native/rebuilt DWARF checks160/176/1208-byte extents and element layout. Conservative direct-CFG row tags verify eight-byte indexed origins/reverse steps, correct0/4-byte field identities, and four consumer argument pairs from the same row with unchanged pointer registers between paired loads. Calls kill caller-save registers and all tracked memory. Row indices/bounds, arbitrary aliases, array contents and full gameplay equivalence are outside this bounded model. Before DWARF emits no location for these three already-declared arrays; this observation is not a claim that no physical memory existed.
